S52.01.needs: at least one custom assistant already created
S52.01.note: The list is a picker: Enter activates an agent. Edit and remove are typed commands, not buttons in the list.
steps: Start the app with agi, then type /agents and press Enter.
Look for the "Agents" box: each row shows the name, color, scope (project or global), model and description.
Type part of a name in the search line to filter the list, then press Esc to close it.
To remove one, type /agents delete <name> --yes (without --yes it only shows a warning that the delete cannot be undone).
To change one, type /agents set <name> <field> <value>, then /agents show <name> to see the result.
Compare with Expected: open, edit and remove are all reachable, but the list itself has no edit or remove buttons, and Enter activates the agent instead of opening an editor.
S52.01.where: Type /agents (no words after it) in the AGI CLI chat screen. It opens the "Agents" list.

S52.02.needs: a signed-in account with a model for the description form; none for the blank template
S52.02.note: The description form runs a model request. A single word creates a blank template instead.
steps: Type /agents create (with nothing after it) and press Enter to see the "Create new agent" help.
Type /agents create reviews pull requests for risky changes and press Enter.
Wait for "Generating agent configuration..." to finish.
Type /agents and press Enter to check that the new agent appears in the "Agents" list.
For a blank template, type /agents create my-reviewer and press Enter, then check for "Created project agent `my-reviewer` at" in the reply.
Compare with Expected: the new assistant can be created from the product, and it shows up in the list.
S52.02.where: Type /agents create <description> (several words, for an AI-drafted assistant) or /agents create <name> (one word, for a blank template) in the chat screen.

S52.04.note: Expected asks for a form or editor; the product offers one typed command per field instead.
steps: Type /agents set reviewer description Reviews risky pull requests and press Enter, using the name of an assistant you made.
Read the reply: it should say the field was updated.
Type /agents show reviewer and press Enter.
Compare with Expected: the new description shows in the details.
Repeat with another field, for example /agents set reviewer model <model name> or /agents set reviewer tools read_file, search_files.
Note the editable fields listed in the "Fields:" line: description, model, color, tools, disallowedTools, skills, maxTurns, maxBudgetUsd, permissionMode, prompt.
S52.04.where: Type /agents set <name> <field> <value> in the chat screen. There is no form or editor screen; each command changes one field.

S52.06.note: The new name is turned into a lowercase slug, so spaces and capitals are removed in the saved name.
steps: Type /agents rename reviewer code-reviewer and press Enter.
Read the reply: it should say the agent was renamed.
Type /agents and press Enter.
Compare with Expected: the new name is shown in the "name" column of the "Agents" list.
Type /agents show code-reviewer and check the "Agent:" heading.
S52.06.where: Type /agents rename <name> <new-name> in the chat screen, then type /agents to check the list.

steps: Type /agents set reviewer description Reviews risky pull requests and press Enter.
Type /agents and press Enter.
Compare with Expected: the description appears in the list row for reviewer.
Clear it with /agents set reviewer description and check that the row shows "(no description)".
S52.08.where: Type /agents set <name> description <text> in the chat screen, then type /agents to see it in the list.

S52.10.needs: a custom assistant to give instructions to
steps: Type /agents set reviewer prompt You review code for security problems only and press Enter.
Type /agents show reviewer and press Enter.
Check the "Prompt:" section at the bottom of the reply for the new text.
Type /agents reviewer to activate it. The reply should say Agent `reviewer` activated.
Ask a question in the chat and compare the answer with the instructions in Expected.
S52.10.where: Type /agents set <name> prompt <text> in the chat screen, then /agents show <name> to read it back.

S52.16.needs: a model name that this account can use
S52.16.note: If the model cannot be switched, the product prints "model override ignored" instead.
steps: Type /agents set reviewer model <model name> and press Enter, using a model name the product accepts.
Type /agents show reviewer and press Enter.
Check the "model:" line in the reply for the chosen model.
Type /agents reviewer to activate it.
Compare with Expected: the reply should say Agent `reviewer` activated and show "(model: ...)" with the pinned model.
S52.16.where: Type /agents set <name> model <model name> in the chat screen, then /agents show <name>. Model names come from the model list in the product.

S52.17.note: The product has no list of tool names to pick from; the names are typed by hand. The name web_fetch appears in the source, and the picker shows tools: all when no list is set.
steps: Type /agents set reviewer tools read_file, search_files and press Enter.
Type /agents show reviewer and press Enter.
Check the "tools:" line in the reply.
Type /agents set reviewer disallowedTools web_fetch to block one tool, then /agents show reviewer again.
Compare with Expected: the tools line lists only the chosen tools, and the disallowed one appears under "disallowed_tools".
S52.17.where: Type /agents set <name> tools <tool names> in the chat screen, or /agents set <name> disallowedTools <tool names> to block some. Check the result with /agents show <name>.
